description: Found investigating fz-sc8.225. IO.inspect(%{__struct__: S, a: 1, b: [2]}) prints %{__struct__: S, a: 1, b: [2]} on every path; Elixir prints %S{a: 1, b: [2]}. The runtime names a struct only through struct_schemas, which holds a schema only where some code constructs %S{}; add one %S{} anywhere and all three paths print %S{...}. Macro.escape of a struct is exactly this literal ({:%{}, [], [__struct__: S, ...]}), so an escaped default such as MapSet.new([1]) in fz-sc8.144 comes back a plain map. Fix: a %{} literal whose __struct__ value is a written module that declares a struct and whose other keys are exactly that struct's fields lowers as that struct's construction (the same value in Elixir), so the program carries the schema and the value prints, dispatches and types as the struct on every path. Any other map naming a module stays a map. Done when: an oracle fixture (no %S{} elsewhere in the program) prints %S{...} for such a literal and for an unquoted Macro.escape(%S{}) on interp, run and build, and a map missing a field still prints as a map. Proposal: https://claude.ai/artifact/N14ZzKaX8vUSfrX4Uxx58t (ticket B).
title: A map literal that spells a struct builds that struct
